prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create one original museum-quality S1 representative of adult Arthropleura armata for Dino Atlas ages 5–14. Horizontal 16:9, one complete animal in a clean left-facing near-lateral identity view with only about 12 degrees of elevation so the side and upper surface are both readable. Late Carboniferous open firm silt; entire head, every leg run and terminal body end inside frame.
Anatomy lock from current evidence: a very low, broad, flattened myriapod, not cylindrical; roughly two dozen broad trunk tergites, each divided into a central dorsal syntergite and wide left/right lateral paratergites rather than giant overlapping isopod shingles. The collum and first post-head unit may have one leg pair, but every following major diplotergite must visibly carry TWO successive short walking-leg pairs on the near side—two distinct leg bases and two legs per tergite, repeated along the trunk. Show the far-side leg tips offset beneath the body. Legs are short, eight-podomere direction, no centipede forcipules. Round flattened head, exactly two slender seven-segment antennae and exactly two small stalked compound eyes; small restrained mandible/maxilla region, never giant predatory jaws. Posterior segments narrow into one terminal end. Head details are a genus-level cue from small juvenile Arthropleura sp. fossils, not certainty for adult A. armata.
Muted dark umber, moss-gray and irregular rusty mineral variation; no repeated stripes. Reject one leg pair per tergite, modern cylindrical millipede, centipede, giant isopod, trilobite, lobster, insect wings, huge fangs, fantasy spikes, regular stamped plates, duplicated head/tail, cropped anatomy, text, logo, watermark, attack or gore. No named-artist style.
